museum.text: What is the diagnosis of the arrowed lesion?
options: Dilated, tortuous veins bulging under the esophageal mucosa
Dilated, tortuous lymphatics bulging under the esophageal mucosa
Elongated, tortuous arteries bulging under the gastric mucosa
Elongated, ulcerated veins projecting into the gastric lumen
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Lower end of esophagus opened longitudinally showing prominent, bluish, elongated, tortuous, dilated submucosal veins bulging beneath the mucosal surface, pathognomonic of esophageal varices.
museum.keyConcept: Esophageal varices: Submucosal venous tortuosity at the lower esophagus due to portal hypertension.

options: Thickened longitudinal mucosal folds of the lower esophagus
Dilated, elongated, tortuous veins under the esophageal mucosa
Linear ulcers along the lower esophageal mucosa
Fibrous bands crossing the lower esophageal mucosa
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The arrows indicate the dilated, elongated, and tortuous submucosal veins running longitudinally in the lower third of the esophagus.
museum.keyConcept: Esophageal varices: Longitudinal tortuous submucosal venous cords.

museum.text: All of the following are effects of liver cirrhosis EXCEPT:
options: Oesophageal varices at the lower end of the oesophagus
Enlarged, congested spleen with a thick capsule
Dark red spleen with atrophic white pulp
Thickened, fibrosed white portal tracts in the liver
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: All are consequences of liver cirrhosis and chronic venous congestion of the portal system except atrophic white pulp with dark red appearance. In chronic congestive splenomegaly (Banti's disease), the spleen is markedly enlarged and firm with a thick fibrous capsule; cut section shows prominent trabeculae and fibrocongestive red pulp expansion.
museum.keyConcept: Congestive splenomegaly: Markedly enlarged, firm spleen with thickened capsule and fibrocongestive expansion.

options: Chronic peptic ulcer of the stomach
Acute gastric erosion of the stomach
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Stomach opened to reveal a solitary, rounded, sharply punched-out ulcer on the lesser curvature. The mucosal folds radiate towards the margins of the ulcer, and the floor is clean and indurated.
museum.keyConcept: Chronic peptic ulcer: Solitary, punched-out mucosal defect with radiating rugae and clean fibrotic base.

museum.text: The orange arrow points to the mucosa around the ulcer. It appears:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In chronic peptic ulcers, the surrounding mucosa is flattened and smooth, with mucosal rugae radiating towards the ulcer crater due to cicatricial contraction of fibrous tissue in the base.
museum.keyConcept: Peptic ulcer gross margin: Smooth, flat margin with radiating rugae.

museum.text: All of the following describe this ulcer EXCEPT:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: A hard, wide, infiltrating base is the hallmark of a malignant ulcer (gastric adenocarcinoma). Chronic peptic ulcers feature a clean, scarred base limited to the muscularis propria without diffuse infiltration.
museum.keyConcept: Malignant vs benign gastric ulcer: Hard infiltrating base characterizes carcinoma.

options: Chronic peptic ulcer of the pylorus
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Segment of stomach showing marked circumferential mural thickening of the pyloric canal with rigidity and luminal stenosis (linitis plastica type of infiltrating adenocarcinoma).
museum.keyConcept: Infiltrating pyloric carcinoma: Diffuse circumferential mural thickening causing gastric outlet obstruction.

options: Chronic peptic ulcer of the pylorus
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Segment of stomach showing marked circumferential mural thickening of the pyloric canal with rigidity and luminal stenosis.
museum.keyConcept: Infiltrating pyloric carcinoma: Mural infiltration with stenosis.

options: Marked circumferential thickening of the pyloric wall by greyish tumour tissue
Marked circumferential thickening of the pyloric wall by whitish fibrous tissue
Marked localized thickening of the pyloric wall by greyish tumour tissue
Marked localized thickening of the gastric body wall by whitish fibrous tissue
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 3 indicates the marked circumferential thickening of the pyloric wall by infiltrative, greyish-white malignant tumor tissue.
museum.keyConcept: Pyloric adenocarcinoma: Circumferential greyish-white mural infiltration.

options: Mucosal infiltration; marked dilatation of the lumen
Muscle infiltration; marked narrowing of the lumen
Muscle infiltration; marked dilatation of the lumen
Serosal infiltration; marked narrowing of the lumen
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 1 indicates deep infiltration of the muscularis propria by malignant neoplastic glands, and label 2 demonstrates severe stenosis of the pyloric orifice.
museum.keyConcept: Gastric carcinoma: Transmural infiltration with luminal stenosis.

options: Malignant ulcer of the stomach with gastrojejunostomy
Infiltrating carcinoma of the stomach with gastrojejunostomy
Malignant ulcer of the duodenum with gastroduodenostomy
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Specimen showing a large, irregular malignant gastric ulcer with raised everted edges, together with a surgical anastomotic stoma connecting the stomach to an adjacent loop of jejunum (gastrojejunostomy).
museum.keyConcept: Gastric malignancy with palliative gastrojejunostomy bypass.

museum.text: Q13. Labels A, B and C represent respectively:
options: Large ulcer at the pyloric region; opened duodenum and jejunum; normal gastric rugae
Large ulcer at the cardiac region; opened duodenum and jejunum; flattened gastric rugae
Large ulcer at the pyloric region; opened duodenum and ileum; lost gastric rugae
Small ulcer at the pyloric region; opened jejunum and ileum; normal gastric rugae
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Labels show the primary gastric ulcer, the loop of jejunum anastomosed to the stomach, and adjacent mucosa.
museum.keyConcept: Gastrojejunostomy specimen landmarks.

museum.text: The circled lesion is located at the:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The primary ulcer crater is situated along the lesser curvature of the gastric body, the classic site for chronic peptic and malignant ulcers.
museum.keyConcept: Ulcer anatomical location: Lesser curvature of stomach.

museum.text: The  arrow on the right points to:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The arrow points to smooth, flattened gastric rugae adjacent to the lesion.
museum.keyConcept: Gastric mucosal flattening.

options: Raised everted edge; necrotic floor; hard infiltrating base
Flat clear-cut edge; necrotic floor; soft fibrous base
Raised everted edge; clean floor; hard infiltrating base
Flat undermined edge; clean floor; soft fibrous base
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Classic gross triad of a malignant ulcer (gastric adenocarcinoma): raised, rolled, everted margins; rough necrotic floor covered by slough and hemorrhage; and an indurated, widely infiltrating base.
museum.keyConcept: Malignant ulcer triad: Raised everted edges, necrotic dirty floor, and hard infiltrating base.

museum.text: All of the following are true except  EXCEPT:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: A sharply punched-out outline with clear-cut margins is the hallmark of a benign peptic ulcer, whereas a malignant ulcer features irregular, raised, everted borders.
museum.keyConcept: Malignant vs peptic ulcer: Punched-out outline characterizes benign peptic ulcers.

options: Jejunum attached to the duodenum with an artificial opening between their lumina
Jejunum attached to the stomach with an artificial opening between their lumina
Duodenum attached to the stomach with a natural opening between their lumina
Jejunum attached to the stomach with a fistulous tract between their lumina
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The specimen shows a loop of jejunum surgically anastomosed to the greater curvature of the stomach with a wide artificial stoma connecting their lumens (gastrojejunostomy).
museum.keyConcept: Gastrojejunostomy: Surgical stoma between gastric body and jejunal loop.

museum.text: THis lesion is best characterized as:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Solitary, well-delineated mucosal ulcer crater with clean floor and radiating rugae characteristic of chronic gastric peptic ulcer.
museum.keyConcept: Chronic peptic ulcer: Solitary mucosal defect with clean floor.

museum.text: All of the following are true about the ulcer  EXCEPT:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Raised everted edges characterize malignant ulcers (gastric carcinomas). Benign peptic ulcers have flat or overhanging, clear-cut edges.
museum.keyConcept: Ulcer margins: Raised everted edges indicate malignancy.

options: Chronic peptic ulcer with surrounding fibrosis
Infiltrating carcinoma of the pylorus only
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large irregular ulcerated mass in the gastric mucosa with raised, rolled, everted margins and a hard, fixed base.
museum.keyConcept: Malignant gastric ulcer: Large, irregular with everted borders.

options: Chronic peptic ulcer of the stomach
Acute gastric ulcer of the stomach
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Gastric specimen displaying a large malignant ulcer crater with necrotic hemorrhagic debris in the floor.
museum.keyConcept: Gastric adenocarcinoma: Malignant ulceration.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Labels 1 and 2 point respectively to the raised, rolled, everted edge of the malignant ulcer and the rough necrotic floor.
museum.keyConcept: Malignant ulcer anatomy: Raised everted edges and necrotic slough in floor.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Liver surface and cut section studded with large, irregular regenerating nodules of variable size (ranging from 3 mm up to several centimeters) separated by broad, depressed, greyish-white fibrous scar bands.
museum.keyConcept: Macronodular cirrhosis: Coarse regenerative nodules (>3 mm) separated by broad irregular fibrous septa.

museum.text: Label 2 points to the nodules. They are:
options: Multiple, round, less than 3 mm in diameter
Multiple, round, 0.5 to 2 cm in diameter
multiple, round, about 5 cm in diameter
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 2 indicates macronodules which typically measure 0.5 to 2 cm (and can reach 3–5 cm), characteristic of post-hepatitic (HBV/HCV) cirrhosis.
museum.keyConcept: Macronodular cirrhosis nodule size: 0.5 to 2 cm diameter.

options: Low hills and shallow depressions of capsule
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 1 shows the chronic fibrotic thickening of Glisson's capsule over the nodular liver parenchyma.
museum.keyConcept: Cirrhotic liver capsule: Fibrotically thickened Glisson's capsule.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Specimen showing prominent large, variable regenerative nodules separated by broad fibrous depressions.
museum.keyConcept: Macronodular cirrhosis.

museum.text: All of the following are features of this liver EXCEPT:
options: Markedly shrunken with retracted cut section
Normal liver tissue in between the nodules
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In true cirrhosis, diffuse parenchymal disorganization occurs throughout the entire organ; normal hepatic lobular architecture is completely lost, and there is NO normal liver tissue between nodules.
museum.keyConcept: Hallmark of cirrhosis: Diffuse architectural distortion without intervening normal parenchyma.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Display of multi-organ autopsy specimens illustrating the consequences of liver cirrhosis: shrunken nodular liver, congestive splenomegaly, and lower esophageal varices.
museum.keyConcept: Systemic triad of cirrhosis: Nodular liver, splenomegaly, and esophageal varices.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In chronic congestive splenomegaly (Banti's spleen), the spleen enlarges symmetrically while maintaining its characteristic anterior border notch.
museum.keyConcept: Congestive splenomegaly: Symmetrical splenic enlargement with preserved notch.

museum.text: All of the following describe the spleen in  EXCEPT
options: Dark red with atrophic white pulp
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In chronic congestive splenomegaly, the spleen is markedly ENLARGED, tense, firm, and weighs several times normal with a THICKENED, smooth fibrous capsule; it is never shrunken.
museum.keyConcept: Congestive splenomegaly gross features: Markedly enlarged, firm with thickened capsule.

options: Laennec’s cirrhosis with nodular cut section
Macronodular cirrhosis with nodular cut section
Bilharzial fibrosis with white portal tracts
Fatty change with yellow bulging surface
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The arrowed liver specimen shows post-necrotic macronodular cirrhosis with prominent regenerative nodules on cut section.
museum.keyConcept: Macronodular cirrhosis cut section.

museum.text: All of the following are true about the specimens  EXCEPT:
options: The esophagus shows dilated tortuous submucosal veins
The liver shows thickened white portal tracts
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Thickened white portal tracts (pipe-stem fibrosis) are the pathognomonic hallmark of Schistosoma (Bilharzial) periportal fibrosis, whereas in cirrhosis the fibrous tissue forms bands surrounding regenerative nodules.
museum.keyConcept: Cirrhosis vs bilharzial fibrosis: Thickened white portal tracts characterize schistosomiasis.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Liver cut section displaying a background of micronodular/macronodular cirrhosis upon which a large, bulky, yellowish-green, necrotic primary tumor mass (hepatocellular carcinoma) has arisen.
museum.keyConcept: Hepatocellular carcinoma on cirrhosis: Bulky malignant mass superimposed on cirrhotic nodules.

museum.text: All of the following describe the arrowed mass EXCEPT:
options: Greyish with areas of haemorrhage and necrosis
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: A central depression (umbilication) is characteristic of SECONDARY / metastatic liver tumors (due to central ischemia and necrosis). Primary HCC lesions are bulky, expansile, fleshy masses without central umbilication.
museum.keyConcept: Primary HCC vs metastatic nodules: Central umbilication characterizes metastatic carcinoma.

options: Cirrhotic nodules in a macronodular cirrhosis
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The starred lesions represent the background regenerative cirrhotic nodules surrounding the dominant tumor mass.
museum.keyConcept: Background cirrhotic nodules in HCC.

museum.text: The tissue between the nodules is
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The tissue separating the cirrhotic nodules consists of dense collagenous fibrous bands (septa) containing chronic inflammatory infiltrates and proliferating bile ductules.
museum.keyConcept: Cirrhotic septa: Collagenous fibrous bands bridging portal and central areas.

options: Cirrhotic nodules in a macronodular cirrhosis
Cirrhotic nodules in a micronodular cirrhosis
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Liver cut section studded with multiple, discrete, rounded, jet-black to dark brown tumor nodules of varying sizes, characteristic of metastatic malignant melanoma.
museum.keyConcept: Metastatic melanoma to liver: Jet-black pigmented nodules scattered throughout the parenchyma.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hepatic parenchyma containing multiple, ragged, irregular, poorly demarcated necrotic cavities without a formed fibrous capsule, filled with chocolate-colored 'anchovy paste' necrotic liquefied liver tissue.
museum.keyConcept: Early amoebic liver abscess: Multiple irregular necrotic cavities lacking a mature fibrous wall.

options: Multiple, irregular, filled with necrotic liver tissue
Multiple, regular, with thick fibrous walls
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The arrowed cavities are multiple, irregular in contour, and filled with necrotic, liquefied liver parenchyma (anchovy sauce pus) produced by Entamoeba histolytica histolytic enzymes.
museum.keyConcept: Amoebic abscess cavity: Irregular margins filled with liquefactive anchovy-paste debris.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Liver section containing a large, solitary, chronic amoebic abscess cavity encapsulated by a dense, thick, whitish fibrous wall that demarcates it from the adjacent compressed liver parenchyma.
museum.keyConcept: Chronic amoebic liver abscess: Solitary large cavity enclosed by a thick mature fibrous capsule.

museum.text: The cavity wall is lined by:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In chronic long-standing amoebic abscesses, the host mounts a prominent fibroblastic response, producing a thick collagenous fibrous capsule lining the cavity.
museum.keyConcept: Chronic amoebic abscess wall: Mature fibrous encapsulation.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hepatic section displaying a large rounded cystic cavity whose pericyst wall has undergone dense dystrophic calcification, presenting as a hard, rigid, chalky-white, radio-opaque shell.
museum.keyConcept: Calcified hydatid cyst: Dystrophic calcification within the fibrous pericyst capsule.

options: Thick fibrous wall with chalky white calcification
Thick fibrous wall with irregular necrotic lining
Thin fibrous wall with chalky white calcification
Thin fibrous wall with smooth regular lining
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The yellow arrow points to the thick fibrous pericyst demonstrating prominent chalky-white calcified deposits.
museum.keyConcept: Hydatid cyst calcification: Chalky-white calcified pericyst wall.

museum.text: The border of this liver is described as:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The anterior border of this enlarged, fatty liver is blunted and rounded, contrasting with the normal sharp inferior hepatic margin.
museum.keyConcept: Fatty liver border: Blunted, rounded anterior margin.

options: Portal tracts that are thickened, fibrosed and white
Portal tracts that are thickened, fibrosed and yellow
Dilated bile ducts with surrounding fibrosis
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The red arrow points to the portal triads, which are conspicuously expanded by dense, whitish, collagenous scar tissue surrounding intrahepatic portal vein branches.
museum.keyConcept: Symmers' pipe-stem fibrosis: Dense whitish periportal fibrous collars.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Liver cut section displaying broad, dense, whitish fibrous sleeves expanding the portal tracts ('clay pipe-stem fibrosis'). Liver lobular architecture is preserved, and true regenerative nodules are absent.
museum.keyConcept: Bilharzial hepatic fibrosis (Symmers' pipe-stem): Non-cirrhotic portal fibrosis with preserved lobules.

museum.text: The liver tissue between the portal tracts is greyish brown because of:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The hepatic parenchyma appears brownish-grey to slate-grey due to extensive deposition of bilharzial pigment (hemozoin / schistosomulum pigment) engulfed by Kupffer cells and portal macrophages.
museum.keyConcept: Bilharzial pigment: Slate-grey parenchymal discoloration due to macrophage hemozoin.

museum.text: All of the following describe these nodules EXCEPT:
options: Separated by fibrous bands with no normal live
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In bilharzial periportal fibrosis, true regenerative nodules do NOT form, and the hepatic parenchyma between portal tracts remains normal and preserved (non-cirrhotic).
museum.keyConcept: Bilharzial fibrosis architecture: Preserved intervening liver parenchyma without nodular remodeling.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Liver is uniformly enlarged, smooth, with a diffuse bright yellow color, rounded borders, and a greasy, yellowish-tan cut surface that bulges on sectioning.
museum.keyConcept: Hepatic steatosis (fatty liver): Diffusely enlarged, yellow, greasy liver with rounded margins.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Gallbladder is markedly enlarged, elongated, and tense with a thin, translucent wall and pale serosa, resulting from chronic cystic duct obstruction by an impacted stone with absorption of bile and accumulation of clear mucous secretion (mucocele).
museum.keyConcept: Hydrops of gallbladder (mucocele): Distended translucent gallbladder filled with sterile mucus.

museum.text: All of the following describe this gall bladder EXCEPT:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In hydrops of the gallbladder, the wall is markedly STRETCHED, thin, and translucent; a thick, contracted, fibrotic wall is characteristic of chronic calculous cholecystitis, not hydrops.
museum.keyConcept: Hydrops vs chronic cholecystitis: Hydrops features a distended, thin, translucent wall.

museum.text: The lumen of this opened gall bladder is filled with
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In hydrops (mucocele) of the gallbladder, cystic duct obstruction causes the trapped bile pigments to be resorbed by the mucosa, while mucosal epithelial goblet cells continue to secrete clear, watery mucus ('white bile').
museum.keyConcept: Mucocele lumen: Clear, sterile, watery mucinous secretion ('white bile').

options: Cholesterol stone with hydrops of the gall bladder
Hydrops of the gall bladder without stones
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Markedly distended, thin-walled gallbladder containing a single, large, yellowish, oval cholesterol calculus impacted in Hartmann's pouch/cystic duct.
museum.keyConcept: Hydrops with solitary cholesterol stone: Cystic duct impaction leading to mucocele.

museum.text: the arrow points to a complication of this lesion:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The arrow points to the solitary cholesterol calculus firmly impacted in the neck of the gallbladder/cystic duct, precipitating the luminal obstruction.
museum.keyConcept: Cystic duct stone impaction: Mechanical cause of gallbladder hydrops.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Segment of terminal ileum displaying a solitary, blind-ended, finger-like tubular diverticulum arising from the anti-mesenteric border approximately 2 feet proximal to the ileocecal valve.
museum.keyConcept: Meckel's diverticulum: True congenital diverticulum on the anti-mesenteric border of ileum.

museum.text: Label 1 points to a structure that is:
options: Blind-ended, about 10 cm long, on the mesenteric border
Blind-ended, about 10 cm long, on the anti-mesenteric border
Open-ended, about 2 cm long, on the anti-mesenteric border
Blind-ended, about 2 cm long, on the mesenteric border
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 1 indicates Meckel's diverticulum, which arises from the anti-mesenteric border of the ileum as a blind-ending pouch (remnant of the vitelline / omphalomesenteric duct).
museum.keyConcept: Meckel's diverticulum anatomy: Anti-mesenteric blind pouch of terminal ileum.

options: Tuberculous ulcers of the small intestine
Typhoid ulcers of the small intestine
Amoebic ulcers of the large intestine
Bacillary dysentery of the large intestine
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Segment of ileum showing multiple transverse mucosal ulcers oriented perpendicular to the long axis of the bowel (girdle ulcers), with ragged undermined edges and subserosal tubercles.
museum.keyConcept: Tuberculous intestinal ulcers: Transverse 'girdle' ulcers with undermined edges and serosal tubercles.

museum.text: which of the following best describers the ulcers
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Tuberculous ulcers are caused by caseous necrosis within submucosal lymphoid tissue that breaks through the overlying mucosa, creating undermined edges.
museum.keyConcept: Pathogenesis of tuberculous ulcer: Submucosal caseation sloughing through mucosa.

options: Oval, longitudinal, parallel to the direction of the gut
Oval, transverse, perpendicular to the direction of the gut
Oval, transverse, parallel to the direction of the gut
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Intestinal tuberculous ulcers encircle the gut transversely (girdle ulcers) because Mycobacterium tuberculosis spreads circumferentially along the transverse submucosal lymphatic channels.
museum.keyConcept: Tuberculous ulcer orientation: Transverse / perpendicular to gut axis along lymphatics.

museum.text: the yellow arrow points to the ulcer margins. They are:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The margins of intestinal tuberculous ulcers are ragged and characteristically undermined, because caseous necrosis in the loose submucosa extends more widely than the mucosal defect.
museum.keyConcept: Tuberculous ulcer edges: Characteristically undermined margins.

museum.text: which of the following describes these ulcers
options: Caseous material and tubercles in the floor
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The floor of a tuberculous ulcer is ragged, dirty, and studded with yellowish-white caseous tubercles.
museum.keyConcept: Tuberculous ulcer floor: Caseous debris and tubercles.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The arrow points to prominent, enlarged, matted mesenteric lymph nodes with areas of yellowish-white caseation necrosis (tabes mesenterica).
museum.keyConcept: Tabes mesenterica: Matted, caseous mesenteric tuberculous lymphadenopathy.

museum.text: All of the following are features of this specimen EXCEPT:
options: Outer surface studded with tiny yellowish tubercles
Enlarged, matted, caseating mesenteric lymph nodes
Black foci of gangrene with perforations
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Intestinal tuberculosis features strictures, adhesions, and caseation; acute moist gangrene with black perforations is a vascular/ischemic catastrophe (strangulation), not tuberculosis.
museum.keyConcept: Intestinal TB features: Matted nodes, tubercles, transverse ulcers; lacks primary gangrene.

museum.text: The red arrows point to LN that are:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The red arrows indicate mesenteric lymph nodes that are enlarged, fused together into matted conglomerates, and show cheesy caseous necrosis on cut section.
museum.keyConcept: Tuberculous lymph nodes: Matted and caseous.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Resected loop of small intestine demonstrating acute moist gangrene secondary to strangulation at the hernia neck: the loop is swollen, dark purple to black, cold, and friable with lost peritoneal luster.
museum.keyConcept: Strangulated intestinal hernia: Ischemic loop showing acute moist gangrene.

options: Bacillary dysentery of the large intestine
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Intestinal loop showing diffuse, blackish discolouration, severe edema, hemorrhagic infarction, and loss of mucosal lining due to complete mesenteric vascular occlusion.
museum.keyConcept: Moist intestinal gangrene: Dark black, necrotic, foul-smelling bowel segment.

museum.text: the circled area most likely shows:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The circled area demonstrates the sharp, pale, indented constriction rings at the neck of the strangulated loop where the constricting band arrested blood flow.
museum.keyConcept: Strangulation constriction rings: Narrow grooved lines of mechanical pressure at loop neck.

options: Multiple black areas due to gangrene
Multiple oval ulcers with necrotic floor
Multiple areas of dirty greyish membrane
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The arrows indicate extensive patchy to confluent areas of dark black necrosis resulting from tissue putrefaction and iron sulfide formation.
museum.keyConcept: Gangrenous bowel discoloration: Blackish tissue necrosis.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Segment of small bowel showing invagination of a proximal ileal loop (intussusceptum) into the lumen of the immediately adjacent distal ileal segment (intussuscipiens).
museum.keyConcept: Ileo-ileal intussusception: Telescoping of proximal ileum into distal ileal lumen.

options: Invagination of one ileal loop into another
Invagination of the terminal ileum into the cecum
Herniation of an ileal loop through the abdominal wall
Twisting of an ileal loop around its mesentery
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Ileo-ileal intussusception is defined as the telescoping or invagination of one segment of the ileum into an adjacent segment of the ileum.
museum.keyConcept: Definition of ileo-ileal intussusception: Ileum invaginating into ileum.

museum.text: the orange arrow points to the entering loop, which is:
options: Pale, thin, with areas of necrosis
Swollen, bluish, with areas of haemorrhage
Swollen, greyish, with tiny yellow tubercles
Contracted, bluish, with dirty greyish membrane
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The entering loop (intussusceptum) suffers venous obstruction, becoming intensely congested, swollen, cyanotic (bluish-red), and hemorrhagic.
museum.keyConcept: Intussusceptum pathology: Venous congestion, intense swelling, and hemorrhagic infarction.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label A indicates the entering loop of ileum (the inner invaginating tube of the intussusceptum).
museum.keyConcept: Intussusception anatomy: Entering ileal loop.

museum.text: The area circled in orange, shows:
options: Constriction ends of a strangulated loop
Stenosis and fibrous adhesion distal to the intussusception
Stenosis and fibrous adhesion proximal to the intussusception
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The orange circle highlights the constricted neck of the intussusception where mesenteric vessels are compressed.
museum.keyConcept: Constriction neck of intussusception.

museum.text: The arrow at the top right points to
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The arrow points to the entering proximal segment of bowel passing into the receiving sheath.
museum.keyConcept: Entering loop of intussusception.

options: Constriction ends of a strangulated loop
Stenosis and fibrous adhesion distal to the intussusception
Stenosis and fibrous adhesion proximal to the intussusception
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Pathological changes distal to the intussusception include inflammatory adhesions and luminal compromise.
museum.keyConcept: Intussusception complications: Obstruction and fibrous adhesions.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Surgical specimen demonstrating the terminal ileum invaginating through the ileocecal valve into the cecum and ascending colon.
museum.keyConcept: Ileo-cecal intussusception: Terminal ileum invaginated into cecum.

museum.text: The starred structure with the arrow represents:
options: Terminal ileum invaginated into the caecum through the ileocecal valve
Caecum invaginated into the terminal ileum through the ileocecal valve
Ileal loop invaginated into another ileal loop
Appendix invaginated into the caecum through its orifice
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The starred structure represents the invaginated terminal ileum which forms the apex of the intussusceptum advancing into the cecum.
museum.keyConcept: Ileo-cecal intussusception mechanism: Terminal ileum entering cecum via valve.

options: Terminal ileum invaginated into the caecum through the ileocecal valve
Caecum invaginated into the terminal ileum through the ileocecal valve
Ileal loop invaginated into another ileal loop
Appendix invaginated into the caecum through its orifice
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Terminal ileum invaginated into the caecum through the ileocecal valve.
museum.keyConcept: Ileo-cecal intussusception.

options: Moist gangrene of the small intestine
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Vermiform appendix is swollen, turgid, club-shaped, intensely congested, with a dull serosal surface covered by yellowish-white fibrinous and purulent exudate.
museum.keyConcept: Acute suppurative appendicitis: Turgid, congested appendix coated with purulent exudate.

museum.text: All of the following may be seen in this lesion EXCEPT:
options: Yellow plaques on the outer surface
Thick contracted wall with faceted stones
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: A contracted thick wall with faceted gallstones describes chronic calculous cholecystitis, whereas acute appendicitis features acute transmural swelling and purulent exudate.
museum.keyConcept: Appendicitis vs cholecystitis: Appendicitis lacks thick fibrotic contraction and faceted stones.

options: Amoebic dysentery of the large intestine
Bacillary dysentery of the large intestine
Tuberculous ulcers of the large intestine
Fungating carcinoma of the large intestin
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large intestine opened to reveal a diffuse acute fibrino-purulent pseudomembranous colitis: mucosa is intensely congested and coated by a dirty greyish-green, ragged pseudomembrane with superficial mucosal erosions.
museum.keyConcept: Bacillary dysentery: Diffuse acute pseudomembranous inflammation of colonic mucosa.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The arrow points to the dirty greyish-green pseudomembrane (composed of coagulated fibrin, necrotic epithelial debris, and neutrophils) adhering to the inflamed colonic mucosa.
museum.keyConcept: Pseudomembrane in bacillary dysentery: Fibrinopurulent exudate adhering to mucosa.

museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Segment of colon displaying multiple, discrete, rounded to oval mucosal ulcers with characteristically undermined edges, separated by completely normal intervening mucosal patches.
museum.keyConcept: Amoebic dysentery: Discrete ulcers with undermined edges and normal intervening mucosa.

museum.text: The two thin arrows on the left point to:
options: Normal mucosa in between the ulcers
Dirty greyish membrane between the ulcers
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The arrows highlight intact, healthy, pale colonic mucosa between individual amoebic ulcers, in sharp contrast to the diffuse continuous inflammation of bacillary dysentery.
museum.keyConcept: Amoebic vs bacillary colitis: Intact normal mucosa between ulcers in amebiasis.

museum.text: All of the following describe the circled ulcers EXCEPT:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Amoebic ulcers have a soft base composed of necrotic debris and cellular infiltrate; an indurated, hard base is characteristic of carcinoma, not amebiasis.
museum.keyConcept: Amoebic ulcer characteristics: Soft base, undermined edges, and normal intervening mucosa.

museum.text: In this lesion, the irregular ulcer necks are located:
options: In the center of rounded elevated areas of mucosa
In the center of flattened depressed areas of mucosa
At the margins of rounded elevated areas of mucosa
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Early amoebic lesions begin as small submucosal abscesses that elevate the overlying mucosa into rounded domes, with the ulcer neck opening at the center.
museum.keyConcept: Amoebic ulcer formation: Small central mucosal neck opening over submucosal necrosis.

museum.text: On section, the ulcers of this lesion are described as:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: On cross section, amoebic ulcers are classically flask-shaped (or buttonhole-shaped), having a narrow neck in the mucosa and a broad base in the loose submucosa due to lateral lytic spread of trophozoites.
museum.keyConcept: Flask-shaped amoebic ulcer: Narrow mucosal neck with wide submucosal base.

options: Malignant ulcer of the large intestine
Fungating carcinoma of the large intestine
Amoebic dysentery of the large intestine
Bacillary dysentery of the large intestine
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large intestine displaying a bulky, cauliflower-like, friable, fungating exophytic tumor mass projecting into and partially obstructing the lumen.
museum.keyConcept: Fungating colonic carcinoma: Bulky exophytic cauliflower-like mucosal mass.

museum.text: The intestine proximal to this lesion typically shows:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Chronic partial luminal obstruction by an exophytic colonic carcinoma leads to marked muscular hypertrophy and secondary dilatation of the proximal bowel.
museum.keyConcept: Colonic obstruction: Upstream bowel dilatation and hypertrophy.

options: Fungating carcinoma of the large intestine
Malignant ulcer of the large intestine
Chronic peptic ulcer of the rectum
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Colorectal segment opened to reveal an annular, ulcerating malignant mass with raised, rolled, everted margins, a rough necrotic hemorrhagic floor, and a hard infiltrating base.
museum.keyConcept: Malignant colorectal ulcer: Annular ulcerated mass with raised everted borders.

options: Fungating carcinoma of the large intestine
Malignant ulcer of the large intestine
Chronic peptic ulcer of the rectum
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Specimen showing a prominent exophytic, polypoid, fungating malignant neoplasm arising from the mucosal surface of the cecum/colon.
museum.keyConcept: Fungating colorectal carcinoma: Large polypoid mucosal mass.

options: Fungating carcinoma of the large intestine
Malignant ulcer of the large intestine
Chronic peptic ulcer of the rectum
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Fungating exophytic mass in colon.
museum.keyConcept: Fungating colonic carcinoma.

museum.text: The black discolouration of the wall indicates:
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The dark blackish-purple discolouration of the intestinal wall is due to bacterial putrefaction and formation of iron sulfide (FeS) in ischemic, necrotic, gangrenous tissue.
museum.keyConcept: Moist gangrene: Blackish discoloration produced by bacterial iron sulfide.

museum.text: All of the following are features of this disease in the museum specimens EXCEPT:
options: Outer surface studded with tiny yellowish tubercles
Enlarged, matted, caseating mesenteric lymph nodes
Swollen loop with black foci of gangrene
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Tuberculous peritonitis features diffuse peritoneal thickening, matted loops, and tubercles without acute moist gangrenous loops.
museum.keyConcept: Tuberculous peritonitis features: Diffuse tubercles, ascites, and adhesions; lacks primary gangrene.

museum.text: A 45-year-old man with old pulmonary tuberculosis developed abdominal pain, weight loss, fever and diarrhoea. CT showed ascites, mesenteric lymphadenopathy, thickened peritoneum and multiple nodules. This is the gross appearance of his omentum. What is the diagnosis?
museum.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Greater omentum is markedly thickened, contracted into a rolled-up transverse fibrous mass ('omental cake'), and densely studded with innumerable, tiny, greyish-white to yellowish caseous tubercles.
museum.keyConcept: Tuberculous peritonitis ('omental cake'): Thickened fibrotic omentum studded with tubercles.

lab.text: What is the nature of this lesion?
options: Diffuse hepatic fibrosis with regenerative liver nodules
Portal fibrosis with preserved liver architecture, chronic specific inflammation
Biliary obstruction with endogenous pigment deposition
Malignant epithelial tumor of viral oncogenesis
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Liver biopsy displaying expanded portal tracts by dense collagenous fibrous tissue containing bilharzial granulomas, dead calcified Schistosoma ova, and chronic inflammatory cells, with preserved lobular architecture and absence of true regenerative nodules.
lab.keyConcept: Bilharzial hepatic fibrosis: Portal expansion with dead ova and preserved lobular architecture.

lab.text: the circled structure labeled 1 represents
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 1 indicates dead, calcified, shrunken Schistosoma mansoni ova embedded within the periportal fibrous tissue, surrounded by foreign-body giant cells, histiocytes, and eosinophils.
lab.keyConcept: Dead Bilharzial ova: Calcified, oval, brownish egg shells within portal granulomas.

lab.text: Label 3  represents:
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 3 indicates dark brown to blackish granular bilharzial pigment (hemozoin / schistosomulum pigment) engulfed within the cytoplasm of portal histiocytes and Kupffer cells.
lab.keyConcept: Bilharzial pigment: Dark granular hemozoin inside portal macrophages.

lab.text: the area labeled A shows:
options: Expanded portal tract by  Bilharzial granulomas
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Area A demonstrates marked fibrous widening of a portal triad infiltrated by specific granulomatous inflammation surrounding bilharzial ova.
lab.keyConcept: Expanded portal tract in schistosomiasis: Fibrous expansion by granulomas.

lab.text: All of the following are true about the lesion in  EXCEPT:
options: It causes hepatic non-cirrhotic portal hypertension
Ova reach the portal tracts as emboli through the portal circulation
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In pure bilharzial hepatic fibrosis (Symmers' pipe-stem), parenchymal liver functions (serum albumin, bilirubin, coagulation factors) remain PRESERVED for decades because hepatocytes and lobular architecture are intact; liver failure occurs only if viral hepatitis or end-stage cirrhosis supervenes.
lab.keyConcept: Bilharzial fibrosis clinical hallmark: Preserved parenchymal liver functions with non-cirrhotic portal hypertension.

lab.text: (C), indicates:
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label C highlights the surrounding hepatic lobules where hepatocyte cords, sinusoids, and central veins maintain normal spatial orientation.
lab.keyConcept: Preserved lobular architecture in schistosomiasis.

lab.text: What is the nature of this lesion?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: High-power section of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), a malignant epithelial neoplasm derived from transformed hepatocytes.
lab.keyConcept: Hepatocellular carcinoma: Malignant epithelial neoplasm of hepatocyte origin.

lab.text: which of the following describes this photo
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Neoplastic hepatocytes are organized into thick, irregular cords and trabeculae (many cells thick, in contrast to normal 1- to 2-cell thick hepatic plates) separated by sinusoid-like vascular spaces lined by endothelial cells.
lab.keyConcept: HCC trabecular pattern: Thick multicellular hepatocyte cords flanked by sinusoids.

lab.text: The architectural pattern shown is :
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Architectural pattern consisting of widened hepatocyte trabeculae separated by sinusoid-like channels.
lab.keyConcept: HCC trabecular architecture.

lab.text: The architectural pattern shown is
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Neoplastic hepatocytes are arranged in pseudoglandular / acinar structures around central dilated lumina (pseudocanaliculi), mimicking glands.
lab.keyConcept: HCC pseudoglandular/acinar pattern: Neoplastic cells arranged around central lumina.

lab.text: All of the following are features of this legion except
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cytological hallmarks of malignancy include an INCREASED nuclear-to-cytoplasmic (N/C) ratio; a decreased N/C ratio is characteristic of benign, well-differentiated or mature cells.
lab.keyConcept: Malignancy hallmark: Increased N/C ratio, nuclear pleomorphism, and hyperchromasia.

lab.text: which of the following is true
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Neoplastic cells demonstrate a characteristic trabecular architecture with widened liver cell plates.
lab.keyConcept: Trabecular growth pattern in HCC.

lab.text: label 1 and label 2 represent respectively:
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 1 indicates the cellular, pleomorphic malignant hepatoma (HCC) focus, and label 2 indicates the background regenerating cirrhotic pseudolobules.
lab.keyConcept: HCC arising in cirrhotic liver: Tumor focus adjacent to regenerative nodules.

lab.text: all of the following are true about the lesion in EXCEPT:
options: A common predisposing factor in Egypt is HBV and HCV
It is usually preceded by a phase of cirrhosis
It is a malignant epithelial tumor
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is a key oncofetal tumor marker that is characteristically ELEVATED (frequently >400–1000 ng/mL) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma.
lab.keyConcept: HCC tumor marker: Serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is markedly increased.

lab.text: what stain is used, and what do the bluish areas (arrows) represent?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Masson's trichrome special stain stains collagen fibers intense blue or green, clearly outlining the broad fibrous tissue septa bridging between portal tracts and central veins.
lab.keyConcept: Masson's trichrome stain: Blue-stained collagen septa delineating cirrhotic nodules.

lab.text: The areas outlined by the red dotted lines in are:
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The areas encircled by blue fibrous septa represent rounded regenerative nodules (pseudolobules) lacking normal central veins.
lab.keyConcept: Cirrhotic pseudolobules: Regenerative parenchymal islands lacking normal vascular orientation.

lab.text: What is the nature of the lesion
options: Diffuse hepatic fibrosis with regenerative liver nodules
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Definitive histological triad of liver cirrhosis: diffuse parenchymal extinction, dense collagenous bridging fibrous septa, and structural remodeling into round regenerative pseudolobules.
lab.keyConcept: Histological definition of cirrhosis: Diffuse fibrosis with regenerative pseudolobules.

lab.text: All of the following are found here EXCEPT:
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Liver cirrhosis is a chronic progressive disease characterized by mononuclear lymphocytes, plasma cells, and macrophages; dense acute neutrophil infiltration is seen in acute ascending cholangitis or severe alcoholic hepatitis, not uncomplicated viral cirrhosis.
lab.keyConcept: Cirrhotic infiltrate: Chronic mononuclear inflammatory cells, not acute neutrophils.

lab.text: All of the following are true about the lesion   EXCEPT:
options: The commonest cause in Egypt is viral hepatitis
It presents with portal hypertension manifestations
It is a predisposing factor for HCC
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In established liver cirrhosis, progressive hepatocyte loss and architectural distortion lead to severe parenchymal dysfunction (hypoalbuminemia, coagulopathy, jaundice, hepatic encephalopathy).
lab.keyConcept: Cirrhosis pathophysiology: Progressive impairment of parenchymal liver functions.

lab.text: Which of the following best describes the structures indicated by the yellow arrows?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hepatocytes contain a single, large, clear intracytoplasmic lipid vacuole that pushes the nucleus to the periphery of the cell, giving a signet-ring appearance.
lab.keyConcept: Macrovesicular steatosis: Large solitary lipid droplet displacing nucleus to cell margin.

lab.text: What is the nature of the lesion
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hepatic steatosis (fatty liver) is characterized by abnormal intracellular accumulation of neutral triglycerides within the cytoplasm of hepatocytes.
lab.keyConcept: Fatty liver nature: Reversible intracellular triglyceride accumulation in hepatocytes.

lab.text: What is the nature of the lesion
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Intrahepatic cholestasis manifests as abnormal accumulation of endogenous bile pigment (bilirubin) presenting as greenish-brown to yellowish plugs within dilated bile canaliculi and droplet accumulation within hepatocytes.
lab.keyConcept: Cholestasis: Endogenous bile pigment accumulation within canaliculi and hepatocytes.

lab.text: labels 1, 2 and 3 represent respectively:
options: Proliferated bile ductules; bile accumulations; fibrosis and chronic inflammatory infiltrate
Angiomatoids; bile accumulations; fibrosis and chronic inflammatory infiltrate
Proliferated bile ductules; bile accumulations; lymphoid stroma
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The microscopic field demonstrates proliferated, tortuous interlobular bile ductules, yellowish-brown inspissated bile plugs (bile thrombi), and periportal fibrosis with chronic inflammation.
lab.keyConcept: Biliary obstruction histology: Proliferated ductules, bile thrombi, and portal fibrosis.

lab.text: All of the following are true about the lesion EXCEPT:
options: The patient presents with yellow skin and sclera
It may progress to liver cirrhosis
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Complete obstructive (cholestatic) jaundice prevents conjugated bilirubin from entering the intestine, resulting in the absence of stercobilin and producing pale, clay-colored stools; dark stool is seen in hyperbilirubinemia due to hemolysis.
lab.keyConcept: Cholestatic jaundice features: Pale clay-colored stools, tea-colored urine, and pruritus.

lab.text: What is the nature of the lesion
options: Benign encapsulated mixed salivary gland tumor
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Warthin's tumor (papillary cystadenoma lymphomatosum) is a benign, encapsulated salivary gland neoplasm arising almost exclusively in the superficial lobe of the parotid gland.
lab.keyConcept: Warthin's tumor: Benign encapsulated parotid tumor with epithelial and lymphoid components.

lab.text: the red star marks:
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The red star marks a prominent lymphoid follicle with an active germinal center within the dense, mature lymphoid stroma of Warthin's tumor.
lab.keyConcept: Warthin's tumor lymphoid stroma: Dense lymphoid tissue with active germinal centers.

lab.text: The cells lining this legion are
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cystic and papillary spaces in Warthin's tumor are lined by a characteristic double-layered oncocytic epithelium: a luminal layer of tall columnar oncocytes with granular eosinophilic cytoplasm (packed with mitochondria) and a basal layer of cuboidal cells.
lab.keyConcept: Warthin's tumor epithelium: Double-layered oncocytic (mitochondria-rich) epithelium.

lab.text: All of the following are true about the lesion  EXCEPT:
options: It is also called papillary cystadenoma lymphomatosum
It contains chondroid and myxoid stroma
Cystic spaces may show intraluminal papillary projections
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Chondroid and myxoid mesenchymal stroma is the pathognomonic hallmark of Pleomorphic Adenoma (benign mixed tumor), NOT Warthin's tumor (which features oncocytic epithelium in a dense lymphoid stroma).
lab.keyConcept: Warthin's vs pleomorphic adenoma: Chondromyxoid stroma characterizes pleomorphic adenoma.

lab.text: What is the nature of the lesion
options: Benign encapsulated mixed salivary gland tumor
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Pleomorphic adenoma is a benign, encapsulated mixed tumor of salivary glands characterized by a remarkable diversity of epithelial/myoepithelial structures intermingled with mucoid, myxoid, and chondroid mesenchymal-like elements.
lab.keyConcept: Pleomorphic adenoma: Benign mixed tumor with epithelial ducts and chondromyxoid stroma.

lab.text: labels A and B represent respectively:
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Labels indicate ductular/trabecular epithelial structures and surrounding myxoid/chondroid stroma produced by myoepithelial cells.
lab.keyConcept: Pleomorphic adenoma dual histology: Epithelial-myoepithelial units and myxoid matrix.

lab.text: All of the following are true about the lesion EXCEPT:
options: It has epithelial duct-like structures with spindle myoepithelial cells
Its mesenchymal elements include myxoid tissue with chondroid islands
It is most common in the parotid gland
Its stroma is rich in lymphoid follicles with germinal centers
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: A lymphoid stroma with germinal centers is the hallmark of Warthin's tumor; pleomorphic adenoma has a chondromyxoid, hyaline, or osseous mesenchymal stroma.
lab.keyConcept: Pleomorphic adenoma stroma: Chondromyxoid matrix; lacks lymphoid germinal centers.

lab.text: The dashed arrows indicate inflammatory involvement of which structure?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The dashed arrows indicate diffuse infiltration of the muscularis propria by acute inflammatory cells (neutrophils and pus cells), the definitive histological criterion for acute appendicitis.
lab.keyConcept: Acute appendicitis diagnostic hallmark: Transmural neutrophil infiltration into muscularis propria.

lab.text: What is the nature of this lesion?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Acute suppurative (phlegmonous) appendicitis is a classic diffuse suppurative inflammation characterized by extensive neutrophil infiltration throughout all mural layers of the appendix with mucosal necrosis and pus in the lumen.
lab.keyConcept: Acute phlegmonous appendicitis: Diffuse suppurative transmural inflammation.

lab.text: Which of the following best identifies the circled structure?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The circled structure is a prominent mucosal/submucosal lymphoid follicle with a pale germinal center, an anatomical component of normal appendiceal lymphoid tissue that may undergo reactive hyperplasia.
lab.keyConcept: Appendiceal lymphoid follicle: Mucosal lymphoid tissue with reactive germinal centers.

lab.text: All of the following are histopathological findings of this legion EXCEPT:
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Acute appendicitis is an acute non-neoplastic bacterial/obstructive inflammatory lesion; malignant glandular proliferation is seen in adenocarcinoma, not suppurative appendicitis.
lab.keyConcept: Appendicitis vs adenocarcinoma: Acute appendicitis lacks neoplastic glandular proliferation.

lab.text: What is the most likely diagnosis?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Colonic polyp characterized by a smooth rounded contour, abundant edematous lamina propria with chronic inflammatory infiltrate, and multiple cystically dilated, mucus-filled glands lined by bland epithelium (retention polyp).
lab.keyConcept: Juvenile polyp: Hamartomatous retention polyp with cystically dilated mucous glands.

lab.text: Which of the following is the characteristic microscopic finding?
options: Crowded malignant glands invading the muscularis propria
Hyperchromatic dysplastic epithelium with nuclear pseudostratification
Pools of extracellular mucin containing malignant cells
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Characteristic microscopic finding of juvenile polyps: markedly enlarged, cystically dilated colonic glands filled with inspissated mucin and lined by attenuated, non-dysplastic columnar epithelium.
lab.keyConcept: Juvenile polyp microscopic hallmark: Cystically dilated mucus-filled glands.

lab.text: Which of the following best describes the epithelial lining of the dilated glands?
options: Malignant columnar cells with marked atypia
Bland columnar cells with goblet cells
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The dilated glands in juvenile polyps are lined by bland, mature, non-dysplastic columnar absorptive cells and abundant goblet cells without nuclear atypia.
lab.keyConcept: Juvenile polyp epithelium: Bland, mature columnar and goblet cells lacking dysplasia.

lab.text: All of the following are true about this legion polyps EXCEPT:
options: They are also called retention polyps.
They commonly occur in children under 5 years.
They may present with rectal bleeding.
They contain a fibrovascular core with or without inflammation.
They are benign neoplastic polyps characterized by epithelial dysplasia.
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Juvenile polyps are non-neoplastic HAMARTOMAS (retention polyps); adenomatous polyps are the benign neoplastic polyps that feature epithelial dysplasia.
lab.keyConcept: Juvenile vs adenomatous polyp: Juvenile polyps are hamartomas without dysplasia.

lab.text: What is the most likely diagnosis?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Colonic mucosal polyp exhibiting crowded, branching, tubular epithelial glands lined by dysplastic columnar epithelium with nuclear stratification, hyperchromasia, and loss of goblet cells (tubular adenoma).
lab.keyConcept: Adenomatous polyp (tubular adenoma): Neoplastic polyp displaying epithelial dysplasia.

lab.text: Which of the following is the hallmark feature of this lesion?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The absolute hallmark and defining criterion of an adenoma is epithelial dysplasia (nuclear hyperchromasia, enlargement, elongation, pseudostratification, and active mitoses).
lab.keyConcept: Adenoma hallmark: Epithelial dysplasia (the precancerous milestone).

lab.text: All of the following are true about this legion EXCEPT:
options: Their characteristic glands are lined by bland, non-dysplastic epithelium with goblet cells.
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Adenomatous polyps are DEFINED by dysplasia and loss of normal differentiation (depletion of goblet cells); bland non-dysplastic epithelium characterizes hyperplastic or juvenile polyps.
lab.keyConcept: Adenoma histology: Dysplastic epithelium with goblet cell depletion.

lab.text: Which of the following best describes the nature of this lesion?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Colonic adenomas are benign neoplastic epithelial lesions that serve as well-established premalignant precursors for colorectal adenocarcinoma via the adenoma-carcinoma sequence.
lab.keyConcept: Adenomatous polyp nature: Benign neoplastic precancerous precursor of adenocarcinoma.

lab.text: Which of the following statements about this legion  is CORRECT?
options: They are always malignant at the time of diagnosis.
High-grade dysplasia may progress to carcinoma in situ and then adenocarcinoma.
They are characterized by cystically dilated glands without dysplasia.
They are always associated with a fibrovascular core.
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In the adenoma-carcinoma sequence, accumulation of genetic mutations (APC, KRAS, TP53) drives progression from low-grade dysplasia to high-grade dysplasia, intramucosal carcinoma, and invasive adenocarcinoma.
lab.keyConcept: Adenoma-carcinoma sequence: Progression from dysplasia to invasive adenocarcinoma.

lab.text: Which of the following features is most characteristic of the epithelial changes indicated by the arrows?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Characteristic dysplastic features of adenomatous epithelium: elongated, hyperchromatic, crowded nuclei stacked in multiple layers (pseudostratification) occupying the basal half to full thickness of the epithelium.
lab.keyConcept: Dysplasia features: Nuclear pseudostratification, hyperchromasia, and enlargement.

lab.text: identify the structure indicated by the right arrow.
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The right arrow points to adjacent uninvolved normal colonic mucosa with straight, parallel, test-tube crypts containing abundant goblet cells.
lab.keyConcept: Colonic mucosa: Normal parallel crypts lined by mature goblet cells.

lab.text: A histopathological examination of a colonic tumor reveals malignant glands of variable size and shape. The glands are lined by one or more layers of malignant cells and invade through the basement membrane into the submucosa.
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: High-power microscopic examination showing irregular, crowded, back-to-back malignant glands infiltrating through the muscularis mucosae and invading the submucosa, diagnostic of invasive adenocarcinoma.
lab.keyConcept: Invasive colorectal adenocarcinoma: Irregular malignant glands infiltrating the bowel wall.

lab.text: What is the most likely diagnosis?
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Malignant epithelial neoplasm composed of atypical glands invading a desmoplastic fibrous stroma in the wall of the colon.
lab.keyConcept: Colonic adenocarcinoma: Invasive malignant glands within desmoplastic stroma.

lab.text: All of the following are true about this legion EXCEPT:
options: It may present with bleeding per rectum.
It may present with irregular bowel habits.
It may appear as an ulcerating, fungating or infiltrating mass.
Its malignant glands may invade the submucosa.
Its epithelial cells show no nuclear atypia.
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Adenocarcinomas are malignant neoplasms whose lining cells characteristically display marked cytological atypia: pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, prominent nucleoli, and atypical mitotic figures.
lab.keyConcept: Adenocarcinoma cytological features: Marked cellular and nuclear atypia.

lab.text: All of the following are characteristic microscopic features of this legion EXCEPT:
options: Glands variable in size and shape
Cystically dilated glands lined by bland columnar
lab.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cystically dilated glands lined by bland, non-dysplastic epithelium are the hallmark of juvenile retention polyps, whereas adenocarcinomas feature crowded, irregular, back-to-back malignant glands.
lab.keyConcept: Adenocarcinoma vs juvenile polyp: Invasive carcinoma features irregular atypical glands, not bland cystic glands.
